LESSON: TRUST CHRISTIAN VALUES

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: By the end of the Sub strand, the ● Learners to read the story of the unforgivin
Topic 4.4: Trust Christian Values

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Trust Christian Values. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when people talk taken ● Learners to discuss effects of talking about others about you?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify people they can trust for their ●

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TRUST CHRISTIAN VALUES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Trust Christian Values helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: TRUST CHRISTIAN VALUES
Study Trust Christian Values like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify people they can trust for their ●

What this means
In this part you learn to identify people they can trust for their ●. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify people they can trust for their ●.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Trust Christian Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify people they can trust for their ●. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Trust Christian Values is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Trust Christian Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify people they can trust for their ●)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Trust Christian Values to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify people they can trust for their ●.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Trust Christian Values from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Trust Christian Values: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Trust Christian Values?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when people talk taken ● Learners to discuss effects of talking about others about you?
2. Why is it wrong to others for harmonious living obey………….” talk about others?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Trust Christian Values means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify people they can trust for their ●.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
